clue.text: Atrocious acts on WWI battle site, riots perhaps

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of the first British battle of the First World War

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of the words that come before it may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A First World War battlefield is the scene of horrors, rioting among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word putting the battle first; 'perhaps' scrambles the two words after the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Monstrosities are outrageous, appalling deeds, which is what atrocious acts are.

clue.text: Essential to score goal with rabbit (no artist) playing against duck

indicators.note: against means placed beside, here the last piece set next to the anagram
playing suggests the letters are performing in a new arrangement
no says the following abbreviation is to be removed from the word before it

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: A footballer scores with a rabbit, while some bird gets in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops the artist from the rabbit before 'playing' scrambles what remains with the goal; 'against' sets the duck beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an obbligato is a part that must not be omitted, so it is essential to the score.

clue.text: The smell of money, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, a piece of money

explanation.surface: Asks what wealth smells like.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is a smell, especially a pleasant one.

clue.text: Turns taken with these turners, audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the word is heard, in a non-rhotic British accent

parts.note: rotors are the parts of a machine that turn

explanation.surface: A rota tells people when their turn comes, said with a pun on spinning parts.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech the final R of ROTORS is silent, so it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotas are schedules setting out whose turn it is, so turns are taken by them.

clue.text: 9's musical technique?

parts.note: 9 is a famous serial killer, so his technique would be a serial one; the musical term is the twelve-tone method of composing in series

explanation.definitionFit: Serialism is the compositional technique of Schoenberg and others built on ordered series of notes.

clue.text: I set theme, spinning record when work's done

indicators.note: spinning means the letters of the words before it whirl into a new order

explanation.surface: A DJ chooses a theme and plays a record once the day's work is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' looks like the record turning on the deck, but it rearranges I SET THEME.
explanation.definitionFit: A timesheet is a record of the hours an employee has worked.

clue.text: Lack of interest evident, though 9 could be around the bend

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go round the next piece
could be says the letters of the number word might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: the number in the clue read as the word nine
a U-bend is a bend in a pipe, so U

explanation.surface: Boredom shows, though the killer at 9 down might be mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 points to the Ripper, but here it is just the word NINE, rearranged as ENNI by 'could be'; 'around' wraps it round U. 'evident, though' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a weary boredom, a lack of interest in anything.

clue.text: Artist demanding women, having to metamorphose, getting more twisted, suspect finally suggested to have been…

parts.note: to metamorphose is to change, or alter
more twisted, in the sense of perverted, is sicker

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An artist with a taste for women, changing and growing more depraved, is a suspected killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 9 down: the painter was proposed by some writers as Jack the Ripper. 'demanding', 'having to', 'getting' and the closing words link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was a British painter of the late nineteenth and early twentieth century.

clue.text: … using cipher, kept in jug (but he never was!)

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters are put inside the vessel

parts.note: a jar is a jug or pitcher

indicators.note: using, in the sense of encoding with, says the words are to be scrambled

explanation.surface: Continues 8: the suspect, written in code, locked in jail, which the real killer never was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is slang for prison, a nod to the killer never being caught; 'using' scrambles the two words before the comma and 'in' puts them inside the jug.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack the Ripper was never caught or jailed, so he is the one who never was in jug.

clue.text: In the locality about 2.10 am (imprecisely)

indicators.note: imprecisely says the letters are not given in their exact order

parts.note: 2 is BI (two, as a prefix) and 10 is TEN

explanation.surface: Someone is somewhere nearby at roughly ten past two in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The time is read as BI, TEN and AM, and 'imprecisely' shuffles them; 'about' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the immediate surroundings, as in ambient noise or temperature.

clue.text: King takes Middle Easterner to a European country

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
an Omani is a person from Oman in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A monarch takes a visitor from the Gulf to a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Soil taken from mountain top

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Earth has been removed from a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: To taint something is to soil or contaminate it.

clue.text: Deserved response to bottom-pinching: criticism for unsophisticated humour

parts.note: a slap in the face is what someone who pinches a bottom deserves
stick is informal for criticism, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: A slap and a telling-off for groping, set against crude comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' as criticism is British informal usage: to give someone stick is to criticise them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, a low form of humour.

clue.text: Cook in pan

definitions.meaning: to cook meat or vegetables in an oven
to criticise harshly, as a critic pans a show

explanation.definitionFit: Roast means to cook in an oven and also, informally, to criticise someone severely.

clue.text: Crime not on for artist, non-starter, though he keeps the money

indicators.note: not says the word that follows is to be taken away

parts.note: treason is the crime of betraying one's country
taken as written

indicators.note: non-starter says the first letter of the artist is dropped

parts.note: Albrecht Durer was a German Renaissance artist

explanation.surface: A club's money man is a sound choice, not a criminal or an artist who fails.
explanation.walkthrough: TREASON without ON leaves TREAS; DURER without its first letter gives URER. 'for' and 'though' link.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the official in charge of an organisation's funds.

clue.text: Lace with speed for a plant

parts.note: to spike a drink is to lace it with alcohol or a drug
a rush is a burst of speed

explanation.surface: A drink is spiked with amphetamine to produce some plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like the drug, adding to the drink-lacing picture, but it simply means haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike-rush is a sedge-like plant of wet places, genus Eleocharis.

clue.text: Match examples, those taken away?

parts.note: to suit is to match or go well with
cases are instances or examples

explanation.surface: Matching specimens, which some people carried off?
explanation.definitionFit: Suitcases are what travellers take away with them on holiday, a cryptic hint.

clue.text: When given general anaesthetic, I don't know the way to avoid traffic

parts.note: a patient under anaesthetic is said to be under
pass is what a quiz contestant says when they do not know

explanation.surface: Someone anaesthetised confesses ignorance of a route around the cars.
explanation.definitionFit: An underpass is a road or path running beneath another, letting people avoid the traffic.

clue.text: Similarity of compounds, one part solid with lead removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
some means a part of something

indicators.note: with lead removed says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a prism is a geometric solid

explanation.surface: Chemicals look alike, one component being a solid that lacks lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the metal but means the first letter: PRISM loses its P, leaving RISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Isomerism is the existence of compounds sharing a formula but differing in structure.

clue.text: No entrance to farm or house

indicators.note: no entrance to says the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a stud is a farm for breeding horses
taken as written

explanation.surface: There is no way into the farm or the farmhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal house from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Carriers soundly sleep on beds

indicators.note: soundly says the words are heard, not read

parts.note: a nap is a sleep and sacks are beds, placed one on the other

explanation.surface: Porters sleep deeply on their beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like deep sleep, but signals that NAP SACKS is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Knapsacks are bags carried on the back, so they are carriers.

clue.text: For the record, white short by two points

indicators.note: short by says the letters that follow are missing from the word

parts.note: albumen is egg white
E and N are two points of the compass

explanation.surface: Officially, an egg white lacks a couple of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing record.

clue.text: Food which makes us hiccup to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dish that gives diners hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese food of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Fight in ditch

explanation.definitionFit: Scrap is informal for a fight and also means to get rid of something.

clue.text: Father has pole for seductress

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Dad has a Polish lover who is a temptress.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Sirens lured sailors to ruin, so a siren is a seductive woman.

clue.text: Actress Julia Roy to rest anyway

parts.note: Roy suggests Rob Roy, the Scottish outlaw, so his first name Rob

indicators.note: anyway says the letters can be put any way at all

explanation.surface: An actress tells a man called Roy to take a break regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob Roy MacGregor was a famous Scottish outlaw, so Roy brings Rob; 'anyway' rearranges REST to ERTS, and 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Julia Roberts is the American film actress of Pretty Woman.

clue.text: Washing powder required for one top

parts.note: Surf is a brand of washing powder
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Laundry detergent is needed for a single shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Surf is a British brand of laundry detergent.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface of something is its top layer.

clue.text: 1 pi? Not to suspect 8, for example

indicators.note: Not says the letters of the following word are to be left out
suspect says the letters are dubious and must be rearranged

parts.note: 1 refers to the answer at 1 across, monstrosities
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled maths query that ends up describing the painter at 8.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of 1 across and PI, remove T and O, and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert worked in the impressionist style, so he is one example of the type.
